name: WV-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+20 partisan lean strongly favors the incumbent
Riley Moore's large fundraising edge ($751K vs $44K cash on hand)
Prediction markets price Moore at ~97% to win
No polling or expert ratings to challenge the fundamentals
model.rationale: WV-02's R+20 lean, Riley Moore's incumbency and dominant fundraising advantage, and markets pricing him near 97% all point to a safe Republican hold. Challenger Ace Parsi's modest war chest gives little reason to move off the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any unexpected polling showing Parsi within single digits, or a major outside-spending surge on his behalf, would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
West Virginia's 2nd District is a deeply Republican seat, with a partisan lean of roughly R+20, and first-term incumbent Riley Moore is running for reelection. Moore has raised over $1.3 million and holds about $751,000 in cash, while Democratic challenger Ace Parsi has raised about $134,000 with roughly $44,000 on hand. No outside groups have meaningfully engaged in the race on either side.

No public general-election polling or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets give Moore about a 97% chance of winning. The district's lean, the incumbent's financial edge, and the lack of any visible challenger momentum make this a safe Republican seat, with the main uncertainty being the wide error band that comes from having no polling at all.
